title: Low Engine Oil Pressure
shortDescription: Engine oil pressure below safe minimum — shutdown to protect engine.
fullDescription:
Kubota GR/T/ZG series lawn tractors with liquid-cooled diesel or gasoline engines monitor oil pressure via a pressure sender. E01 is logged when pressure drops below 10 PSI at idle or 25 PSI at governed speed, triggering automatic shutdown to prevent bearing damage.

Top the oil reservoir and verify with a mechanical gauge before returning to service — sender faults are common in older units.

fixSteps.title: Check oil
fixSteps.instruction: Level mower on flat ground, top up with Kubota-spec oil to full mark.

fixSteps.title: Verify with mechanical gauge
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sender, install mechanical gauge — should read 40-60 PSI at 3000 RPM.

whenToCallPro: If oil and sender are verified good and pressure is still low — oil pump/engine internal service needed.

faq.a: Kubota 10W-30 or 15W-40 depending on climate — consult the operator's manual.

title: Coolant Over-Temperature (Diesel)
shortDescription: Engine coolant temperature above safe threshold.
fullDescription:
Kubota diesel-powered tractors (T series, GR series) monitor coolant temp. E02 triggers above 104 °C (220 °F). Common causes: low coolant, plugged radiator with grass/chaff, failed water pump, stuck thermostat.

Let engine cool at least 30 minutes before opening radiator cap to avoid steam burns.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off, allow to cool 30 min minimum.

fixSteps.title: Clean radiator
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out fins with compressed air from fan side outward.

fixSteps.title: Top off / flush coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Use Kubota Super UDT or equivalent 50/50. Flush at 2-year interval.

whenToCallPro: If water pump is suspect — dealer service.

faq.a: Only if phosphate-free. Kubota Super UDT is safer.

title: PTO Clutch Engagement Failure
shortDescription: PTO clutch not engaging — blade will not spin.
fullDescription: E03 reflects an electromagnetic PTO clutch that is not energizing or has failed to output rotation. Common causes: failed PTO switch, blown 20A fuse, or worn clutch plates. The clutch has an air gap spec of 0.010-0.018" and will drag once worn beyond that.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect fuse box for PTO fuse — replace if blown.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity test PTO switch; replace if failed.

fixSteps.title: Adjust/replace clutch
fixSteps.instruction: Measure air gap with feeler gauge; adjust or replace clutch assembly.

whenToCallPro: Clutch replacement requires puller tools — dealer service.

title: Safety Interlock — Seat
shortDescription: Seat switch reporting operator not seated.
fullDescription: Kubota lawn tractors require operator-seated signal for engine start and PTO engagement. E04 indicates the seat switch is open. Inspect switch, harness, and ensure operator is fully seated.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Measure continuity — should close when depressed.

faq.a: No — safety feature required by standards.

title: Transmission Neutral Not Detected
shortDescription: HST pedal / neutral switch not in correct start position.
fullDescription: Kubota HST tractors require the hydrostatic pedal to be centered and the neutral switch closed to start. E05 flags when switch does not report neutral. Adjust HST pedal linkage per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Center pedal
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure HST pedal released to neutral detent before start.

fixSteps.title: Adjust linkage
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen neutral switch, position so striker engages at pedal center.

whenToCallPro: Dealer if linkage adjustment doesn't resolve.

faq.a: Yes with proper oil service — 400 hours interval for HST fluid.

title: Charging System Fault
fullDescription: Kubota charging systems target 13.8-14.6 V at operating RPM. E06 triggers on over- or under-voltage. Common causes: failed regulator, worn alternator brushes (diesel), or corroded battery cables.

fixSteps.title: Test charging
fixSteps.instruction: Engine at rated RPM — should read 13.8-14.6 V at battery.

fixSteps.title: Replace regulator
fixSteps.instruction: Swap regulator/rectifier if output below 13 V or above 15 V.

faq.a: Group 51R or U1R depending on model.

title: Fuel Filter Water Separator Warning
shortDescription: Water detected in diesel fuel filter bowl.
fullDescription: Diesel Kubotas include a water-separator filter with a sensor. E07 indicates water accumulated at the bottom. Drain immediately via the bowl petcock; running with water will destroy injectors.

fixSteps.title: Drain water separator
fixSteps.instruction: Open petcock until clean fuel flows, close tightly.

faq.a: Not recommended — Kubota engines prefer ULSD.

title: Hydrostatic Transmission Pressure Low
shortDescription: HST fluid pressure below operational threshold.
fullDescription: Kubota hydrostatic transmissions monitor charge pressure. E08 means pressure below spec — typically low fluid, clogged filter, or worn charge pump. Do not continue driving.

fixSteps.title: Check fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Top up with Kubota Super UDT2 to full mark.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Change HST filter per service schedule.

whenToCallPro: If pressure stays low after service — pump rebuild.

faq.a: Newer Super UDT2 is backwards compatible and specified on current models.

title: Glow Plug / Cold Start Fault (Diesel)
shortDescription: One or more glow plugs open-circuit — hard cold starts.
fullDescription: Kubota diesels use glow plugs for cold start. E09 means one plug is open. Engine may still start but slowly and with white smoke. Replace plug to restore cold start performance.

fixSteps.title: Test plugs
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance — good plugs read 0.5-1.5 Ω.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed plug
fixSteps.instruction: Torque to 15 Nm; do not over-torque.

whenToCallPro: Only if a plug snaps in head — extraction is delicate.

faq.a: Recommended — similar age means others likely near end of life.

title: Deck Drive Belt Broken
shortDescription: Mower deck belt broken or derailed.
fullDescription: Kubota RCK-series decks use a single V-belt driving multiple spindles. E10 (on monitored models) or no-blade-rotation symptom flags belt failure. Inspect idler pulleys — a seized pulley shortens belt life dramatically.

fixSteps.title: Remove deck
fixSteps.instruction: Lower to lowest position, disconnect PTO shaft, pull deck out.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pulleys
fixSteps.instruction: Spin each by hand — grinding = bearing failure.

fixSteps.title: Install new belt
fixSteps.instruction: Route per sticker diagram, verify idler spring tension.

title: Parking Brake Not Set
shortDescription: Starting blocked — parking brake not engaged.
fullDescription: Kubota safety interlock requires park brake engaged to start. E11 flags when switch reports brake released.

fixSteps.title: Engage brake
fixSteps.instruction: Pull lever fully up until latched.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: OEM replacement if continuity test fails.

title: Air Filter Restriction (Diesel)
shortDescription: Intake vacuum sensor reports filter restriction.
fullDescription: Kubota diesels include an intake vacuum indicator. E12 or filter service light signifies restriction. Replace per service interval (100-200 hrs).

fixSteps.title: Inspect filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and tap out; if still dirty, replace.
